findings.title: import() calls run eagerly at module load, so nothing is actually lazy
findings.body: Each entry is `import("./x")` evaluated when the object literal is created, so every app module starts loading as soon as `appStore` is imported, regardless of whether it is used. The async wrapping therefore adds no lazy-loading benefit on the server or in client bundles. Entries should be thunks (`() => import("./x")`) and callers should invoke them on demand. Any rejected import is also created up front, so a broken app module can surface as an unhandled rejection even if nothing ever awaits it.

findings.title: Making the forEach callback async moves getCalendar errors out of the try/catch
findings.body: Before this change, `getCalendar` was synchronous, so a throw inside it was caught by the surrounding try/catch and logged. Now the callback is async and the `await getCalendar(...)` and `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` promises are not awaited by `forEach`, so rejections become unhandled promise rejections and the try/catch never sees them. The cancellation work also runs fire-and-forget, so the reschedule returns before calendar/video deletion finishes. The same pattern is in packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts.

findings.title: requestReschedule fires async calendar/video deletions without awaiting them
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...)` discards the promises returned by each callback. The mutation then sends the reschedule email and returns while the `getCalendar` lookup and the `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` calls are still running. Any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection, and the client cannot know whether the old calendar event was actually removed. Use `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` and await it.

findings.title: Async forEach pushes into apiDeletes after it has already been awaited
findings.body: Inside the recurring-cancellation branch, `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` pushes to `apiDeletes` only after an asynchronous await. `forEach` does not wait for these callbacks, so `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs before the pushes happen. Those deletions are never awaited, their errors are unhandled, and the response can report success while calendar events are still being deleted. Replace the forEach with a for...of loop or `Promise.all` over the credentials.

findings.title: Adapter creation is now sequential and awaits each app in a loop
findings.body: `getVideoAdapters` used to build adapters synchronously in one pass. It now awaits each app import one at a time in a `for` loop, so N credentials cost N sequential module-load round trips. Resolving the apps with `Promise.all` would preserve ordering and avoid the serialized waits.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials stores un-awaited getCalendar promises as the calendar value
findings.body: `getCalendarCredentials` is still synchronous, but `getCalendar` now returns a Promise, so `calendar` is a Promise on every returned item. Any consumer that checks `if (!calendar)` or uses the value as a Calendar synchronously will be wrong. A rejected `getCalendar` promise (for example from a failing CalendarService constructor) is also only handled when `getConnectedCalendars` later awaits it, so the rejection can be reported late or unhandled. The function should be made async and should await the calendar, or the field type should be updated to match.
